answer: Spatial Beacon Witnessing: each agent must broadcast a radio beacon whose signal is cross-checked by three nearby agents in different locations; the onyx hardware module that signs the beacon is bound to a fixed physical site, so an operator cannot clone it across sites without detectable timing drift. Fabricating N identities therefore requires N physical installations plus ongoing site leases. A meadow region's beacons anchor rural agents, while jade-tagged modules mark industrial zones, preventing central pooling.
